name: Townscape Quality in Shenyang Fangcheng (SBE + Semantic Differential)
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (45 places in and around the main streets of the Fangcheng historic and cultural district, Shenyang, each as four Baidu street views at 90° steps: ahead along the road, right, behind and left; 2016–2022 captures).

Original study: Tang, Wang & Lyu (2026), Buildings 16(7), 1455. On four main streets of Fangcheng, 87 sampling points were photographed in four directions in April 2025 (348 photos). 110 participants (42 in person, 68 online residents of Shenyang) rated each point's four views for visual preference on a 7-point scale (1 very unattractive, 7 very attractive), standardised as scenic beauty estimation (SBE) z-scores. 34 participants with architecture or planning backgrounds rated six semantic-differential pairs from −2 to +2: conflict–coordination, monotonous–colourful, blurry–sharp, fragmented–coherent, superficial–profound and unattractive–attractive.

Differences from the original study: (1) Baidu street views of 45 places (sampled on a grid inside the district, so some side streets are included) replace the authors' 348 photos of 87 points; each participant sees 20 random places. (2) The SBE rating and the six SD pairs are asked together for each place; in the paper they came from two separate groups. (3) Each SD pair carries a short question written from the paper's Table 1 descriptions. (4) Each place stays on screen for 5 seconds before ratings unlock; the paper projected slides in person.
author: Tang, Wang & Lyu

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: place_set
elements.title: The places (four views each) shown to this participant, in order

elements.name: attractiveness_sbe
elements.title: How attractive is this place?
elements.description: One trial per place (key = place id; the four views are recorded as shown). SBE rating; standardise per participant (z-scores) before averaging, as in the paper.

elements.name: coherence
elements.title: Coherence: how similar are the visual attributes of the scene?
elements.description: One trial per place (key = place id; the four views are recorded as shown). SD scale: −2 very poor … 0 average … +2 very good.

elements.name: color_richness
elements.title: Colour richness: do the building facades show a variety of colours?
elements.description: One trial per place (key = place id; the four views are recorded as shown). SD scale: −2 very poor … 0 average … +2 very good.

elements.name: iconic
elements.title: Iconic: how clearly does the scene convey historical and cultural content?
elements.description: One trial per place (key = place id; the four views are recorded as shown). SD scale: −2 very poor … 0 average … +2 very good.

elements.name: continuum
elements.title: Continuum: are the elements arranged with an orderly, patterned regularity?
elements.description: One trial per place (key = place id; the four views are recorded as shown). SD scale: −2 very poor … 0 average … +2 very good.

elements.name: historicity
elements.title: Historicity: how strongly is the scene connected to the historical narrative?
elements.description: One trial per place (key = place id; the four views are recorded as shown). SD scale: −2 very poor … 0 average … +2 very good.

elements.name: attractiveness_sd
elements.title: Attractiveness: does the space make you want to visit it?
elements.description: One trial per place (key = place id; the four views are recorded as shown). SD scale: −2 very poor … 0 average … +2 very good.
